positions.invalidation: Cover if AUDNZD holds above 1.27 or if a Hormuz-driven oil bid sends the cross to a new high while NZDUSD breaks 0.55.
positions.thesis: AUDNZD at 1.2456 is a five-year extreme while NZDUSD still sits in the cheap tail at 0.5627. That cross has stretched far beyond a 30-basis-point Australia versus New Zealand 10-year gap, and it is the only concentrated, asymmetric swing on a firm tape. Short the cross as a real swing; oil remaining bid is the accepted tax, not a reason to stay flat. CORRA March stays closed: 2.55 cash versus 2.925 is the same leftover path already booked into the event-implied print, not a new dislocation…

pms.thesis: Australian-kiwi is still a crowded elevated cross at 1.2445 after a bounce from 1.2417, with kiwi washed out on the dollar and no fresh Australian policy shock. The swing still has room toward 1.20-1.22 on a multi-week horizon; cheaper oil does not reverse Australia's relative premium enough to close that gap. Cash-versus-March leftovers in SOFR and CORRA are already in the tape and do not clear a new rates book versus sitting in the existing 300 million cross. Being behind on the scoreboard is not a reason to layer correlated receive risk or to cut a working short that has not reached the realization zone.

pms.thesis: Canada March still embeds about 40 basis points of unused tightening versus cash 2.53, and the oil break to Brent 94.62 is a growth-impulse fade that supports the receive rather than a reason to pay. Australian-kiwi remains elevated at 1.2445, so the tactical short still has a mean-reversion path as long as a kiwi smash does not drive the cross to new highs. I am not adding US leftover, dollar-yen, or Australian-Canada: those either duplicate beta already in the book or sit at levels that no longer improve the adverse path after oil cheapened.

pms.thesis: Australian-kiwi is still elevated at 1.2445 after bouncing from 1.2417, so the existing ten-million short retains a swing path if the cross leaves that extreme toward the recent distribution. Fresh tickets in kiwi-dollar, Australian-Canada, dollar-yen, or March leftovers would expand risk into a mid-range oil cross, a stretched yen, or a two-way 39 to 40 basis-point cash-versus-March strip. Official overnight on shocked capital is the hurdle those new ideas fail; the working ten-million cross does not need to be enlarged.
